QGIS Training Module 1 Welcome to ForestPlots course on digital data collection! This course aims at providing principal researchers and field leaders the tools to collect data digitally in the field. It relies on QGIS and QField softwares, respectfully for computers and tablets. For this course, you will need: * a computer running on Windows, ideally Windows 11 (this training is not yet available for Mac users) * an Android tablet * a cable to link the computer and the tablet (usually USB-A and USB-C, or double USB-C) * an internet connection Can everyone please introduce their experience with digital data collection or data collection in general? Advantages and Risks of a Tablet Can everyone please share the advantages and risks they could face with digital data collection? Advantages Risks Time saver Misoneism Less prone to error Electronic waste Workflow more fluid Cost More flexible Data loss (including theft) Less paper Difficult access to electricity Data spatialisation Summary of Digital Data Collection Now that we are aware of the advantages and risks of digital data collection, we can start the technical training, structured around the main components of digital data collection:
Module 2 Accessing ForestPlots What is ForestPlots? How to access ForestPlots data?

Module 2 Accessing ForestPlots When re-censusing a plot, you need access to the data from the previous censuses in order to make a field sheet, find the plot, and collect the data. You can find everything you need on ForestPlots.net.   What is ForestPlots? ForestPlots.net is a database where you can securely store, manage and analyse tropical forest plot data.   ForestPlots.net stores and serves stem data and metadata for multi- and single-census plots in forests and savannas, including trees, lianas, species, demography, traits and soils. How to access ForestPlots data? In order to access the ForestPlots data, you must Read the code of conduct, Register to have an account on ForestPlots here, and Email the associated country data officer to ensure the account is granted and to receive the necessary training to use ForestPlots. Note: Nika Gorski is the data officer for Africa data. Only once you have completed these steps will you be able to access data to ForestPlots and produce field sheets. If you haven’t fully completed these steps, you can still move on to Module 3 and 4 to install the necessary software on your laptop and tablet.
Module 3 How to set up your laptop

Module 3 How to set up your laptop Whether you have a ForestPlots account, you now need to set up your computer and your tablet. You will use your computer to create the surveys and your tablet to execute them. While seemingly boring, the next steps are crucial: if executed properly, they will save us a tremendous amount of issues. Therefore, please take your time so we can stay organised from the beginning. QGIS is a geographic information system software. In order to install QGIS on your computer, please follow these steps: 1. Click here to access the download package. If you feel generous, you can make a contribution to QGIS or skip to download (orange button Skip it and go to download). 2. Once you passed the donation page, download the most recent Long Term Release (currently Download LTR 3.40). Do not download the Latest release, it is not needed for what we do and is more likely to come with bugs. 3. Once you have downloaded the QGIS installation file, open it and follow the instructions. We advise you to keep the default and recommended set-up options. 4. Congratulations, you have installed QGIS on your computer! You can now launch it (be patient, QGIS may take some time to launch) and should soon see a similar interface: 5. Click on the Extensions menu and select Installer/Gérer les extensions. 6. Type ‘QField Sync’ in the research bar of the pop-up window. 7. Tick the box near QField Sync, just below the research bar, and close the pop-up window. 8. Click on the Extensions menu, a QField Sync sub-menu should now be present.
Module 4 How to set up your tablet

Module 4 How to set up your tablet QField is an open-access application for spatial data collection and edition. Here, we assume that you already set up your tablet with a Google account that grants you access to the Google Play Store. In order to install QField on your tablet, please follow these steps: 1. Go to the tablet homepage. 2. Open the Play Store.   3. Click on the Sign in symbol. 4. Either sign in with your own Google account (not recommended) or create an account with a clear name and address. For instance, you can paste the name of your project and country or institution. Choose a secured password that you are also able to remember. It is good to store it somewhere safe and share it with a couple of colleagues. 5. Welcome to the Play Store, you can click on Not now. 6. Type ‘qfield’ in the search bar. 7. Click on QField symbol and then Install it. 8. Once installed, Open QField. 9. Welcome to QField, your computer and tablet configuration is over, we can now start collecting data!

So before diving in to collect data and create a QField project, let’s learn how to move documents between your two devices. 1. Create a folder on your computer called QGIS_training, and save this folder somewhere that you know how to get to and will navigate to often. 2. Save this a picture of a very common tree in the Republic of Congo into your QGIS_training folder: tree.png. Do you know what kind of tree it is? 3. Connect your tablet to your computer via the cable. 4. In your files on the bottom left of your screen, you will see a new device appear. For example, in the image below when an Apple iPad was plugged into the device, it appeared.   5. Copy your QGIS_training folder. 6. Paste your QGIS_training folder into the tablet area of your device. 7. Disconnect your tablet from your computer. Is the image on your tablet? 8. This time download a pdf document and save it to your computer and move it to the tablet: ForestPlot Codes. When you are done, disconnect the tablet from the laptop and check that the pdf is on your tablet. 9. Now to move a document from the tablet to your computer, you do the same thing but in reverse. With your tablet disconnected from your computer, take a photo of your neighbor (with their permission) and save it to your QGIS_training folder with their name. 10. Connect your laptop and tablet via the cable and move the image from the tablet’s QGIS_training folder into the QGIS_training folder on your laptop. 11 Disconnect your laptop and tablet. On your computer do you have an image of a tree, a pdf, and an image of your neighbor in your QGIS_training folder? And that’s how to move documents between your laptop and tablet.

Module 7 Setting up the survey How does QGIS work?

Module 7 Setting up the survey Learning objectives learn what a QGIS package is how to set up a QGIS package and the QGIS survey on your laptop   How does QGIS work? We learnt to collect data on QField but how do you create the survey in the first place? 1. Create a new folder qgis_training_example2 in the Documents section of your file explorer. 2. Create a subfolder named layers in the folder you created at the previous step. 3. Download the following files: Tree flags, Diameter values, POM values, Style, Fieldsheet. 4. Copy them in the layerssubfolder you created at step 2. 5. Open QGIS. 6. Click on the Projet menu and then Enregistrer sous…. 7. Save your project under the name qgis_training_example2.qgz in the qgis_training_example2 folder created at step 1. 8. Click on the Projet menu and then Propriétés.   9. In the Général tab, verify that length and area units follow the metric system. 10. Click on the Couche menu, then Ajouter une couche and finally Ajouter une couche de texte délimité…. 11. Click on the three points facing Nom de fichier. Another window pops-up, go to the layers subfolder you created at step 4 and select the first .csv file. 12. In Format de fichier, select the right separator. The table columns should be conserved, you can check in the section Echantillon de données. Verify that Détecter les types de champs is unticked. Verify that Pad de géométrie (juste la table) is ticked. 13. Click on Ajouter. 14. Repeat for all the .csv files in the layers subfolder. 15. Then go to the GeoPackage tab on the right-hand panel and click on Nouveau. 16. Select treesheet_training.gpkg from the layers subfolder in the pop-up window. 17. Click on the Connecter button, then on treesheet_training (highlighted in blue) and finally on Ajouter. 18. Click right on the treesheet_training layer and then click on Propriétés. 19. Click on Style in the left bottom corner of the pop-up window (it does not matter in which tab) and then click on Charger le style. 20. Click on the three dots symbol in the pop-up window. 21. Select training_style.qml and then click on Ouvrir. 22. You are now back to the previous pop-up window where you need to click on Charger le style. 23. You are back to the Propriétés window, click on Ok. 24. Your now have to format your QGIS project for export: click on Extensions, then QFieldSync, and finally Configurer le projet actuel. 25. Go to Export par câble and check that every layer is classified as Copy in the Action section. 26. Click on Extensions, then QFieldSync, and finally Paquet pour QField. 27. Verify that the QField package will be stored as closest as your computer root as possible, then click on Créer. 28. Connect the tablet to your laptop and allow sharing of the tablet data, then go to your QField package location. 29. Copy the QField package and paste it at the root of your tablet. You can now proceed open your project on the tablet (see Using QField survey for a reminder on how to proceed) and collect data!
Module 8 Configuration du questionnaire Comment fonctionne QGIS?

Module 8 Configuration du questionnaire Objectifs d’apprentissage Découvrir ce qu’est un package QGIS Apprendre à configurer un package QGIS et le questionnaire QGIS sur votre ordinateur portable Comment fonctionne QGIS? Nous avons appris à collecter des données sur QField, mais comment créer le questionnaire? 1. Créez un nouveau dossier nommé qgis_training_example2 dans le dossier Documents de votre explorateur de fichiers. 2. Créez un sous-dossier nommé layers dans le dossier créé à l’étape précédente. 3. Téléchargez les fichiers suivants: Tree flags, Diameter values, POM values, Style, Fieldsheet. 4. Copiez-les dans le sous-dossier layers créé à l’étape 2. 5. Ouvrez QGIS. 6. Cliquez sur le menu Projet puis sur Enregistrer sous…. 7. Enregistrez votre projet sous le nom qgis_training_example2.qgz dans le dossier qgis_training_example2 créé à l’étape 1. 8. Cliquez sur le menu Projet, puis sur Propriétés. 9. Dans l’onglet Général, vérifiez que les unités de longueur et de surface sont bien exprimées en unités métriques. 10. Cliquez sur le menu Couche, puis sur Ajouter une couche et enfin sur Ajouter une couche de texte délimité…. 11. Cliquez sur les trois points en face de Nom de fichier. Une nouvelle fenêtre s’ouvre; accédez au sous-dossier layers créé à l’étape4 et sélectionnez le premier fichier .csv. 12. Dans Format de fichier, sélectionnez le séparateur approprié. Les colonnes du tableau doivent être conservées; vous pouvez le vérifier dans la section Échantillon de données. Assurez-vous que Détecter les types de champs est décoché. Assurez-vous que Pad de géométrie (juste la table) est coché. 13. Cliquez sur Ajouter. 14. Répétez l’opération pour tous les fichiers .csv du sous-dossier layers. 15. Accédez ensuite à l’onglet GeoPackage dans le panneau de droite et cliquez sur Nouveau. 16. Sélectionnez treesheet_training.gpkg dans le sous-dossier layers de la fenêtre contextuelle. 17. Cliquez sur le bouton Connecter, puis sur treesheet_training (en bleu) et enfin sur Ajouter. 18. Faites un clic droit sur la couche treesheet_training, puis cliquez sur Propriétés. 19. Cliquez sur Style en bas à gauche de la fenêtre contextuelle (peu importe l’onglet), puis sur Charger le style. 20. Cliquez sur l’icône à trois points dans la fenêtre contextuelle. 21. Sélectionnez training_style.qml, puis cliquez sur Ouvrir. 22. Vous revenez à la fenêtre contextuelle précédente; cliquez de nouveau sur Charger le style. 23. Vous êtes de retour dans la fenêtre Propriétés. Cliquez sur OK. 24. Vous devez maintenant formater votre projet QGIS pour l’exportation: cliquez sur Extensions, puis sur QFieldSync, et enfin sur Configurer le projet actuel. 25. Allez dans Exporter par câble et vérifiez que chaque couche est bien définie sur Copie dans la section Action. 26. Cliquez sur Extensions, puis sur QFieldSync, et enfin sur Paquet pour QField. 27. Vérifiez que le package QField est enregistré au plus près de la racine de votre ordinateur, puis cliquez sur Créer. 28. Connectez la tablette à votre ordinateur portable et autorisez le partage de données, puis accédez à l’emplacement du package QField. 29. Copiez le package QField et collez-le à la racine de votre tablette. Vous pouvez maintenant ouvrir votre projet sur la tablette (consultez la section [Utilisation du sondage QField] pour un rappel de la procédure) et collecter les données !
Module 9 You’ve got data to store! Saving data onto a hard drive Saving data onto a computer

Module 9 You’ve got data to store! Learning objectives Get the data safely onto your device or hard drive Understand what the output of the data is   So, you’ve successfully made a QGIS survey and collected your data. Now onto potentially the most important step of this entire process: making sure that you don’t lose all of the data that you just collected. Saving data onto a hard drive You spent a tough day collecting data in the field, it is now time to store this data in several places to mitigate risks. 1. Open the Play Store, type ‘fv file manager app’ in the research bar and click on Install in the right panel. 2. Once FV File Manager is installed, you can click on Ouvrir. 3. In the notification pop-up, click Don’t allow. 4. Click Do not consent in the personal data use pop-up window. 5. Click on the Files symbol in the right-hand side. 6. Connect your hard drive. 7. Go to your hard drive location, here T7 Shield. Click on the three verticals dots in the right-hand corner and select New folder in the drop-down menu. 8. Give a name with today’s date in YYYYMMDD format, for instance 20260112_sauvegarde. Click OK. 9. Click on Galaxy Tab Active4 Pro on the left panel. 10. Click on Android folder. 11. Click on data folder. 12. Click on ch.opengis.qfield folder. 13. Click on files folder. 14. Click on Imported projects folder. 15. Select qgis_training_example2 by keeping your finger on it, click on the three dots in the top right corner and click on Copy to. 16. Go to the folder you created at step 8 on your hard drive (today 20260112_sauvegarde) and click on COPY in the bottom left corner. 17. Your day’s work is now safely stored in the hard drive. This step must be repeated every night and on a second hard drive. Saving data onto a computer 1. Go to the tablet Internal storage in your computer file explorer and click on the Android folder. 2. Click on data folder. 3. Click on ch.opengis.qfield folder. 4. Click on files folder. 5. Click on Imported projects folder. 6. Copy qgis_training_example2. 7. Go to the folder where you initially created your QGIS project. Create a dump folder. 8. Paste the qgis_training_example2 from step 6 in the dump folder. 9. Double-click on the QGIS project to open it. 10. Once QGIS is launched, open the Extensions menu, select QFieldSync and then Synchroniser depuis QField. 11. Click on the three dots symbol in the top right corner of the pop-up window. 12. Select the folder you pasted at step 8 then click on Sélectionner un dossier. 13. Click on Synchronisation. 14. Point colours has changed: the data has arrived. 15. Click right on the treesheet_training layer, select Exporter and then Sauvegarder les entités sous…. 16. Verify that XSLX is selected in the Format menu, then click on the three dots symbol. 17. Write the future file name beginning by today’s date, for instance 20260112_qgis_training_example2.xlsx, then click on Enregistrer. 18. Click OK. You can go to the storage location and verify that you got your data back!
